item.title: Gold Body Accused of Enabling Deaths at Tanzanian Gold Mine
item.description: The London Bullion Market Association’s certification program served as a “thick smokescreen” that enabled serious abuses at a Tanzanian gold mine where two men died, lawyers alleged at the start of a London trial that could threaten its existence. Lawyers for the two families argue that the gold body’s decisions had a direct effect on the use of violence at the mine. Holding the body accountable for the deaths could pose an existential threat to the association and its Responsible Gold Guidance scheme, which aims to ensure that supply chains are free of human rights abuses and conflict, they added.

item.title: Regulatory and Supervisory Modernisation Principles: Consultation report
item.description: To remain effective, regulatory and supervisory frameworks must keep pace with the dynamic financial sector and be forward-looking and adaptive to current and future material risks. Many financial authorities in FSB member jurisdictions have been reviewing their regulatory and supervisory frameworks to pursue various objectives, including evaluating whether they facilitate sustainable economic growth and remain forward-looking and adaptive to current and future material risks. In this context, the FSB is proposing eight high-level principles for modernisation, addressed to financial authorities.

item.title: G20 Implementation Monitoring Review: 2026 report
item.description: This report is the second report produced in the context of the G20 Implementation Monitoring Review (IMR), a strategic review of the FSB’s work to encourage and monitor the implementation of international financial reforms. This report analyses whether and how the way the FSB develops, drafts, and presents policies affects the implementation of those policies. Looking at international reforms developed by the FSB after the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, the report finds that national circumstances – including legal frameworks, market structure, and political capacity – are the main reason why implementation has been uneven.

item.title: FSB consults on high-level principles for regulatory and supervisory modernisation
item.description: The first report sets out eight high-level principles for financial authorities in FSB member jurisdictions to apply in their efforts to ensure regulatory and supervisory frameworks are forward-looking and responsive to new vulnerabilities, technologies, offerings and economic conditions. Press enquiries: +41 61 280 8477 [email protected] Ref: 13/2026 The Financial Stability Board (FSB) today published two reports: Regulatory and Supervisory Modernisation Principles: consultation report and G20 Implementation Monitoring Review: 2026 report . As financial authorities around the globe pursue such modernisation efforts, these principles should promote alignment and contribute to keeping regulatory and supervisory frameworks effective and responsible.

item.title: In casualty ILS motivations are key, timelines must be realistic: Trahan, Calidris
item.description: Casualty insurance-linked securities transactions are complex and require strong alignment, which makes finding strategic partners and understanding their motivations key, while at the same time given the complexity of arrangements such as casualty sidecars, realistic timelines are important, Philippe Trahan of Calidris Investment Partners said yesterday. Trahan, Co-founder and Co-CEO of insurance-focused investment manager Calidris Investment Partners, was speaking during a casualty ILS focused panel session at the ILS Bermuda Convergence 2026 conference yesterday. As a company with a focus on opportunities in these longer-tailed areas of insurance and reinsurance, Trahan noted that Calidris recognises the time required to both get comfortable with counterparties and asset managers involved in casualty transactions, as well as being cognisant of the time needed to get to well-structured and aligned deal outcomes.

item.title: PICC P&C’s new $12m Great Wall Re is the first Hong Kong sidecar ILS issuance
item.description: PICC Property and Casualty Company Limited has now reported that its new US $12 million issuance of insurance-linked securities under its Great Wall Re Limited special purpose insurer is actually a quota share reinsurance sidecar, the first in Hong Kong, designed to provide protection to its offshore wind power property insurance book on the Chinese Mainland. This morning PICC Property and Casualty Company has said that the US $12 million (HK $94m) Great Wall Re ILS issuance is “the first issuance of insurance-linked securities with a “sidecar” structure in the Hong Kong market,” and the first issuance of sidecar insurance-linked securities by any domestic Chinese insurance company. The insurer said this is “another innovative practice for the company to use the international capital market to spread insurance risks after the successful issuance of disaster bonds in Hong Kong in 2022.” Being a sidecar, the underlying subject reinsurance arrangement with this US $12 million Great Wall Re deal is a quota share, or proportional reinsurance, transferring the risks to capital market investors on that basis.

item.title: Porch Group to acquire Allied Trust’s insurance carrier and MGA
item.description: Porch Group, a homeowners insurance and vertical software platform, and Porch Insurance Reciprocal Exchange (the Reciprocal) have entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Allied Trust’s managing general agency (MGA) and insurance carrier, respectively. Following closing, Allied Trust is expected to operate under the same structure as Porch Group’s existing insurance business, while the Reciprocal will own the insurance carrier, collect premiums and pay claims, commissions, reinsurance costs and fees to Porch Group for operating services. Under the agreements, Porch Group will acquire Allied Trust’s managing general agent (MGA) and captive reinsurance entity for an aggregate base purchase price of USD 95 million.

item.title: Video: Dialogue, depth and delivery vital to re/insurer relationships, says Swiss Re’s Nikhil da Victoria Lobo
item.description: In the current, very competitive reinsurance operating landscape, the importance of stability and consistency have been key, but the executive emphasised that consistency doesn’t mean doing the same things, but “keeping a very open dialogue, working with an open solution mindset, and finding ways to deliver to clients.” In terms of what makes a really productive insurer and reinsurer relationship, da Victoria Lobo highlighted dialogue, depth, and delivery. This was the message from Nikhil da Victoria Lobo, Head of P&C for Western & Southern Europe and the Middle East & Africa at global reinsurer Swiss Re, in a video interview with Reinsurance News ahead of the annual Baden-Baden meeting . As the global reinsurance industry heads to Baden-Baden, the January renewals will of course be a big topic, and against a backdrop of a complex and increasingly interconnected risk landscape, dialogue, depth, and delivery are key to a productive insurer and reinsurer relationship.

item.title: Verisk estimates Isaias insured losses at $1-2bn, driven largely by wind damage
item.description: Verisk’s Catastrophe and Risk Solutions business has estimated insured industry losses to onshore property from Hurricane Isaias at between $1 billion and $2 billion, with wind damage expected to account for the vast majority of losses. Verisk explained that the estimate covers wind and privately insured storm surge losses from Isaias’ Florida Panhandle landfall. According to the firm, the most severe wind damage occurred west of Isaias’ landfall location, particularly in Florida’s Santa Rosa and northeastern Escambia counties.

item.title: CVS Settles Justice Department Case Over Opioid Prescriptions for $315M
item.description: The Justice Department settled a similar case in August against rival pharmacy chain operator Walmart, which agreed to pay $50 million to resolve a 2020 lawsuit alleging it unlawfully dispensed opioid prescriptions. CVS Health has agreed to pay $315 million to resolve allegations that the pharmacy chain operator unlawfully filled medically unnecessary prescriptions for addictive opioid painkillers, the US Justice Department said on Oct. “Today’s settlement is a significant milestone in the Justice Department’s efforts to combat the opioid epidemic by cracking down on pharmacies who unlawfully fulfill prescriptions for controlled substances,” Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward said in a statement.

item.title: AI Models May Soon Self-Replicate Across Smart-Home Devices, Anthropic Warns
item.description: Anthropic said small AI models could be months away from self-replicating across internet-connected devices, raising the possibility of AI botnets spreading quickly, fighting takedown attempts and even breaking into data centers to turbocharge their growth. It added that the models were able to replicate across a simplified test network. Anthropic said its experiments showed that models with 30 billion parameters or fewer can already perform many of the individual tasks required for self-replication, although they struggle to complete the entire process reliably.

item.title: Fleets, Insurers Struggle With Telematics Data
item.description: Fleets and insurers now have access to telematics data but struggle to convert it into actionable insights that reduce risk. SambaSafety's fourth annual telematics report , based on survey responses from 740 fleets, insurers, and brokers, indicates that 53% of fleets struggle to interpret or act on their telematics data. In 2025, data showed that 48% of insurers said convincing large fleets to share their telematics data is a top challenge.

item.title: Simon Helps Push Eastern Pacific Hurricane Activity to Record
item.description: The eastern Pacific has set a record for hurricane activity as Hurricane Simon lashes Mexico’s west coast and another storm threatens to form. The basin had produced 68.5 hurricane days as of Tuesday morning, surpassing the previous record of 68.25, according to Phil Klotzbach, a hurricane researcher at Colorado State University. “We should add several more hurricane days this week with Simon and very soon to be Trudy,” Klotzbach said by email.

item.title: Three arrests in major FCA operation against criminal insider dealing ring
item.description: The FCA has conducted a major operation to disrupt a suspected organised criminal group for engaging in insider dealing and money laundering. Steve Smart, executive director of enforcement and market oversight at the FCA, said: 'Insider dealing is a serious threat to the integrity of our markets. Working with partners, we will continue to use all the powers at our disposal to crack down on serious and organised crime groups engaged in market abuse.' item.title: Verisk estimates Hurricane Isaias insured onshore property losses in $1bn to $2bn range
item.description: Verisk, a catastrophe risk modelling and data analytics specialist, has now issued an initial industry insured loss estimate for recent hurricane Isaias, saying that onshore property losses from the storm could reach $2 billion. Verisk’s initial industry loss estimate includes losses from wind and privately insured storm surge, as a result of hurricane Isaias’ landfall in the Florida Panhandle. Cotality (formerly CoreLogic), estimated that insured losses from wind and storm surge from hurricane Isaias will be in the $2 billion to $3 billion range.

item.title: ILS investors need to speak up and ask for alternative model views: Karen Clark
item.description: At the ILS Bermuda Convergence 2026 conference today, Karen Clark, CEO and Co-founder of catastrophe risk modelling specialist Karen Clark & Company, urged the insurance-linked securities community and its investors to ask for alternative model views to be included in the deal flow that comes to market. “I think one of the things is, investors need to speak up that you do value alternative views, second generation models. During a panel discussion about how catastrophe modelling can be reimagined, Clark highlighted that ILS deal flow is typically concentrated around views of risk from the main vendor models.

item.title: Mid-single-digit billions of dollars loss from Isaias unlikely to affect P&C re/insurer credit profiles, says Fitch
item.description: A wide rage of insurers and reinsurers are expected to be impacted by Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall as a Category 2 storm in the Florida Panhandle on October 9th, but while the event is expected to drive moderate economic and insured losses, Fitch says it is “not likely to affect credit for rated property/casualty (P/C) (re)insurers.” Hurricane Isaias peaked as a Category 3 major hurricane over the Gulf before increasing wind shear weakened it on approach, eventually making landfall as a Category 2 storm with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph, although has now been downgraded to a tropical storm. In affected areas like Florida, Alabama, Georgia, and The Carolinas, Fitch expects the storm to result in moderate economic and insured losses, estimating that industry losses could reach the mid-single-digit billions of dollars. “The storm’s reduced intensity at landfall is expected to result in more manageable insured losses,” says Fitch.

item.title: Etude Launches E&S Carrier with $100M Surplus
item.description: Etude launched Etude Specialty Insurance Company, a technology-driven excess and surplus lines carrier for commercial property and casualty. Etude Specialty is domiciled in Nebraska, has more than $100 million of surplus, and will write in all 50 states. Using its own capital, with surplus currently in excess of $100 million, Etude Specialty can shape coverage, pricing, and policy language to solve complex insurance needs.

item.title: FAA Tells US Airlines to Exercise Caution in Saudi Arabia Flights, Citing Safety Risks
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration told US airlines to exercise caution when flying to or over Saudi Arabia, citing safety threats tied to ongoing military activities and navigation system interference. In September 2025, FedEx launched its first dedicated flight into Saudi Arabia. R iyadh airport remains closed to flights through at least 5 p.m.

item.title: Sammons introduces Criterion Wealth Management brand
item.description: Sammons Financial Group has introduced Criterion as the new name for its wealth advisory holding company, marking its continued expansion beyond insurance and annuities. Criterion brings together Beacon Capital Management, NorthRock Partners, and Wealthcare, which collectively have more than $27 billion in assets under management or advisement. Led by president Michael Mock, Criterion plans to grow through acquisitions and investments in technology, talent, and advisor capabilities.

item.title: Abacus partners with Retirable
item.description: Abacus Global Management has partnered with Retirable to connect clients with retirement planning services and integrate its LifeARC lifespan modeling technology into Retirable’s platform. After clients complete decisions about their life insurance policies, Abacus and its insurance affiliates will introduce them to Retirable’s licensed fiduciary advisors through warm transfers and scheduled introductions. LifeARC uses AI and 20 years of proprietary Abacus insights to generate lifespan projections.

item.title: Porch Group to acquire Allied Trust
item.description: Porch Group announced that Porch Insurance Reciprocal Exchange and Porch Group have entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Allied Trust’s insurance carrier and managing general agency, respectively. Separately, Porch Group will acquire Allied Trust’s managing general agency and captive reinsurance entity for an aggregate base purchase price of $95 million, consisting of $75 million in cash and an expected $20 million in PRCH shares. Based on Allied Trust’s expected Adjusted EBITDA (Excluding Reciprocal) contribution during the first full year following closing, the transaction represents an acquisition multiple of less than four times for Porch Group.

item.title: Evolving captives becoming strategic platforms for attracting third-party capital: Aon
item.description: Captives are rapidly evolving from risk retention vehicles into strategic capital access platforms, which in turn is beginning to attract third-party capital, according to broker Aon, who emphasises that captive owners are increasingly partnering with external investors to unlock capacity that supports growth initiatives and long-term resilience. Rather than relying exclusively on corporate capital, captive owners are partnering with external investors to unlock capacity that can support larger retention strategies, growth initiatives and resilience objectives.” Aon concludes: “Captives are evolving from risk retention vehicles into capital access platforms, helping organizations connect exposures with the most efficient mix of traditional, alternative and third-party capital.” In a recent article, the broker underscores that captives today offer much more than an opportunity to reduce insurance costs and retain risk, noting that they are now being widely used to help businesses make strategic decisions around capital deployment and long-term resilience.
